Alternative, using the low relatedness set, totally changed the patterns for the Merina. This more stringent kinship filter removed mostly Merina with high .Q1 values, leaving only 12 Merina individuals.

Social group A had lower FIS than social group B, and a lot of correlations between .Q1 and ROH's for the Merina attenuated. The correlations between .Q1 and number of runs, mean length, and total length still remain, but weaker.

```{r}
#Read in Pierron Malagasy metadata

pop_table <- read.table(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable"), sep = "\t", fill = TRUE)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2","FID","Population","V5","V6","V7")

#Remove the "RR"
malagasy$id <- sub("RR.*", "", malagasy$id)

#Find Malagasy entries 
pop_table_sub <- subset(pop_table,pop_table$IID %in% malagasy$id & pop_table$V5 =="Madagascar")

#match up the ID's with pop table metadata
matching_m <- match(malagasy$id, pop_table_sub$IID)

malagasy$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), pop_table_sub$Population[matching_m], malagasy$population)

```

```{r}
malagasy <- malagasy %>% group_by(population)
runs <- gt_roh_window(malagasy,
                            window_size = 15,
                            threshold = 0.05,
                            min_snp = 3,
                            heterozygosity = FALSE,
                            max_opp_window = 1,
                            max_miss_window = 1,
                            max_gap = 10^6,
                            min_length_bps = 1000,
                            min_density = 0.1)
```


# Total number of runs

```{r}
runs_per_indiv <- runs %>% group_by(id) %>% count()

malagasy <- left_join(malagasy, runs_per_indiv, by = "id")
#malagasy$n <- as.factor(malagasy$n)
malagasy$n <- as.numeric(malagasy$n)
malagasy$population <- as.factor(malagasy$population)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data=malagasy, aes(x=id , y=n, fill=population)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  coord_flip()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())+
  labs(x = "Number of runs", y = "ID", fill = "Population")
```


We could test using Kruskal-wallis whether there is a significant diff between 
groups in both number and total length of ROH's. But, this may not answer our 
question. 

We may expect to see higher ROH's in individuals with more Asian ancestry among
the Merina, but we have several confounding effects:

1) Merina with higher African ancestry will be likely to have fewer ROH's anyway, 
as African popualtions have lower homozygosity than other global pops

2) IBD analysis (Alva et al 2022) suggests a bottleneck in the Asian ancestry 
source of all Malagasy people, meaning (if all other things were equal) the Asian 
ancestry component would have more ROH's than the African component 


Ideas:

Anything else we can use as a proxy for caste? Not really, the groups live side by 
side, so location won't help.

Correlations of ROH versus ancestry for all individuals, regardless of ethnic group
Correlations of ROH versus ethnicity for all individuals, regardless of ancestry

Analyse, see how well each explains the data

A model including the effects of both should be the best fit?


Could we remove the Merina, predict based on the correlation of ancestry/ROH's in the
other data where they should fall in ROH distribution given their ancestry, and 
then show that that model alone doesn't account for the inflation in ROH's?

```{r}
annotate_group_info <- function(q_tbl){
  group <- q_tbl %>% dplyr::distinct(id,group) %>% dplyr::pull(group)
  if (length(rle(group)$values)!=length(unique(group))) {
    stop("values in 'group' are not ordered (they should be in consecutive blocks, one per group")
  }
  group_x <- cumsum(table(forcats::fct_inorder(group)))
  segment_data = data.frame(
    x = group_x+0.5,
    xend = group_x+0.5,
    y = rep(0,length(group_x)),
    yend = rep(1, length(group_x))
  )

  get_mid_points <- function (vec){
    (vec[-length(vec)] + vec[-1L])/2.
  }

  list(
  ggplot2::geom_segment(data = segment_data,
                        ggplot2::aes(x = .data$x,
                                     y = .data$y,
                                     xend = .data$xend,
                                     yend = .data$yend),
                        inherit.aes = FALSE),
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(breaks = unique(q_tbl$id)[get_mid_points(c(0,group_x))],
                                labels = names(group_x)),
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1)))
}

order_plot <- function(q_tbl, data, annotate_group = FALSE){
    
  K <- 3

  #q_tbl <- tidy(object, data)
    q_tbl <- q_tbl %>% tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::starts_with(".Q"),
                                           names_to = "q", values_to = "percentage") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(percentage = as.numeric(.data$percentage))

    q_tbl <- q_tbl %>%
      dplyr::group_by(.data$group, .data$id) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(.data$group, .data$id)
    
    
    levels_q <- unique(q_tbl$id)

    q_tbl <- q_tbl %>%
      dplyr::mutate(id = factor(.data$id, levels = levels_q))
    
    plt <- ggplot2::ggplot(q_tbl,
                           ggplot2::aes(x = .data$id,
                                        y = .data$percentage,
                                        fill = .data$q)) +
      ggplot2::geom_col(width = 1,
                        position = "stack")+
      ggplot2::labs(y = paste("K = ", K))+
      #ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = color_mapping)+
      scale_fill_distruct()+
      ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))

    
    if (annotate_group){
      if (is.null(data)){
        warning("no annotation possible if 'gen_tbl' is NULL")
      } else {
        plt <- plt + annotate_group_info(q_tbl)
      }
    }
    plt
  }
   

```

# FIS

FIS Merina as a whole
FIS for non-Merina to compare 


```{r}
malagasy$population <- as.character(malagasy$population)

fis <- malagasy %>% group_by(population) %>% pop_fis(method = "WG17", by_locus = FALSE, include_global=FALSE, allele_sharing_mat = NULL)
fis <- as.data.frame(fis)
fis$population <- rownames(fis)

# rearrange fis column fis in descending order
fis <- fis[order(fis$fis, decreasing = TRUE),]

# Reorder the population variable as a factor based on the descending order of FIS
fis$population <- factor(fis$population, levels = fis$population)

ggplot(fis, aes(x = population, y = fis, fill = population, colour = population, shape = population))+
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
labs(title = "FIS for each population", x = "Population", y = "FIS (WG17)")+
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2")+
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 3, 4, 8)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(title = "Population"),
    colour = guide_legend(title = "Population"),
    shape = guide_legend(title = "Population")
  ) 

```

FIS for the Merina subsets 

```{r}
# subset the malagasy_all dataframe to only the "Merina"
merina <- malagasy_all %>% filter(population == "Merina")

# plot column .Q1 for the merina
ggplot(merina, aes(x = .Q1))+geom_histogram()
```


```{r}
# replace column $group in merina with a factor - those with .Q1 higher than 0.5 are 1 and those lower than 0.5 are 2
merina$group <- ifelse(merina$.Q1 > 0.5, "Social group A", "Social group B")

# calculate FIS by grouping merina by the new column $group and then using group_map
fis_merina <- merina %>% group_by(group) %>% pop_fis(method = "WG17", by_locus = FALSE, include_global=FALSE, allele_sharing_mat = NULL)#

# change fis_merina to a dataframe and make a column $population corresponding to group
fis_merina <- as.data.frame(fis_merina)
fis_merina$population <- rownames(fis_merina)
colnames(fis_merina) <- c("fis", "population")

# add fis_merina to fis
fis <- rbind(fis, fis_merina)

# rearrange fis column fis in descending order
fis <- fis[order(fis$fis, decreasing = TRUE),]

# Reorder the population variable as a factor based on the descending order of FIS
fis$population <- factor(fis$population, levels = fis$population)



ggplot(fis, aes(x = population, y = fis, fill = population, colour = population, shape = population))+
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
labs(title = "FIS for each population", x = "Population", y = "FIS (WG17)")+
  #scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2")+
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 3, 4, 8, 2, 1)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())+
  #scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(title = "Population"),
    colour = guide_legend(title = "Population"),
    shape = guide_legend(title = "Population")
  ) 


```

F: Inbreeding coefficient, calculated as:

F=E(HOM)−O(HOM)N(NM)−E(HOM)/N(NM)−E(HOM)E(HOM)−O(HOM)


```{r}
#Read in Pierron Malagasy metadata

pop_table <- read.table(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable"), sep = "\t", fill = TRUE)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2","FID","Population","V5","V6","V7")

#Remove the "RR"
fis_indiv$IID <- sub("RR.*", "", fis_indiv$IID)

#Find Malagasy entries 
pop_table_sub <- subset(pop_table,pop_table$IID %in% fis_indiv$IID & pop_table$V5 =="Madagascar")

#match up the ID's with pop table metadata
matching_m <- match(fis_indiv$IID, pop_table_sub$IID)

fis_indiv$FID <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), pop_table_sub$Population[matching_m], fis_indiv$FID)

```

```{r}
# plot the distribution of fis_indiv$F for each group of FID

  geom_histogram()+
  facet_wrap(~FID)+
  labs(y = "Count of Individuals", Y = "FIS (F)")

# create a column $total_count in fis_indiv to count the number of individuals in each group
total_count <- table(fis_indiv$FID)
fis_indiv$total_count <- total_count[fis_indiv$FID]



# add total_count number to the top right corner of each facet plot 
ggplot(fis_indiv, aes(x = F, fill = FID))+
  geom_histogram()+
  facet_wrap(~FID)+
  labs(y = "Count of Individuals", Y = "FIS (F)") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  geom_text(data = fis_indiv %>%
              distinct(FID, total_count),  # Extract unique FID and total_count
            aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = paste0("Individuals: ", total_count)), 
            size = 3, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, inherit.aes = FALSE)
```

# Recalculate FIS using plink, this time separating the inferred social groups

If there is assorative mating, FIS should drop when the Merina are considered as two independent populations

```{r}
# take the merina dataset, and rename $population based on $group, "Social group A" will become "Merina_A" and "Social group B" will become "Merina_B"
merina$population <- ifelse(merina$group == "Social group A", "Merina_A", "Merina_B")

# write the merina dataset to a new plink file with gt_as_plink()
gt_as_plink(merina, resrepo::path_resrepo("data/intermediate/Merina"), type = "bed")

# problem - pop names are lost?
# read in Merina.fam
merina_fam <- read.table(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/intermediate/Merina.fam"), header = FALSE)
# remove RR from the IID column
merina_fam$V2 <- sub("RR.*", "", merina_fam$V2)
# match V2 and merina$id and replace the population column in merina_fam with the population column in merina
matching_m <- match(merina_fam$V2, merina$id)
merina_fam$V1 <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), merina$population[matching_m], merina_fam$V1)
# rewrite merina_fam out to merina.fam
write.table(merina_fam, resrepo::path_resrepo("data/intermediate/Merina.fam"), row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

```
